blocks.overview: The case concerns a Colombian citizen seeking refugee protection in Canada, claiming threats from the Los Urabeños paramilitary group. The tribunal examined the claimant's credibility and the viability of an internal flight alternative within Colombia. The claim was rejected as the tribunal found a viable internal flight alternative and no serious risk of persecution.

blocks.issue: Is the claimant credible and has he established a well-founded fear of persecution?
blocks.court_conclusion: The claimant is credible but failed to provide persuasive evidence of ongoing risk or persecution.

positions.text: Claimant testified to threats and persecution by Los Urabeños and fears for his life in Colombia.
Panel found claimant credible but lacking evidence of ongoing risk or investigation outcomes.
Claimant's testimony lacked corroboration; objective evidence outweighed claimant's assertions.

blocks.issue: Is there a viable internal flight alternative (IFA) for the claimant within Colombia?
blocks.court_conclusion: The panel found Tunja to be a viable internal flight alternative for the claimant.

positions.text: Claimant argues IFA is unreasonable due to inability to practice law and risk from Urabeños in Tunja.
Panel found Tunja safe with no Urabeños presence and claimant would not face serious persecution there.
IFA in Tunja is viable; claimant faces no serious risk or unreasonable barriers to relocation.

propositions.text: Claimant is a Colombian citizen seeking refugee protection under sections 96 and 97(1) of IRPA

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 1 states the claimant is a Colombian citizen seeking refugee protection under IRPA, as said by the claimant.

propositions.text: Claimant has a degree from XXXX XXXX University attained in 2004 and worked in that field from 2005 to 2014 in Santa Marta, Colombia
Claimant was involved in XXXX starting with local politics in 1997 and developed further interest later

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 2 states the claimant's education and work history and political involvement, as said by the claimant.

propositions.text: In mid 2013, claimant agreed to help his brother advance his XXXX interest in a XXXX position in Santa Marta for 2015 election

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 3 states the claimant agreed to help his brother's political interest in 2013, as said by the claimant.

propositions.text: Claimant learned his brother and four others were massacred at a farm house in Masinga by Los Urabeños paramilitary group

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 4 states the claimant learned his brother was massacred by Los Urabeños, as said by the claimant.

propositions.text: On XXXX XXXX XXXX 2014, two men identifying as Los Urabeños threatened claimant to leave Santa Marta or be killed
Claimant hid and his lawyer filed a denunciation at Bacrim to investigate the massacre
Claimant received a threatening call from a man claiming to be Los Urabeños aware of the denunciation
Claimant moved to Bogota for 40 days in 2014, returned to Santa Marta, continued receiving threats and filed another denunciation

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 5 states claimant was threatened by Los Urabeños, filed denunciations, moved temporarily, and continued to receive threats, as said by the claimant.

propositions.text: On XXXX XXXX XXXX 2014, police gave claimant Basic Self-Protection Measures document
Claimant sought help from government bodies including Human Rights District Office and Attorney General on XXXX XXXX XXXX 2014

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 6 states police gave claimant self-protection advice and claimant sought help from government bodies, as said by the claimant.

propositions.text: Claimant received no feedback from organizations, moved to Medellin and back to Santa Marta, then left Colombia fearing for life
Claimant travelled via U.S. for 13 days and arrived in Canada on XXXX XXXX XXXX 2015
Claimant and wife separated; wife and son not part of claim

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 7 states claimant left Colombia via U.S. to Canada in 2015, separated from wife, as said by the claimant.

propositions.text: Panel is satisfied claimant established identity on balance of probabilities per passport

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 8 states the panel found claimant's identity established per passport.

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant is not a Convention refugee nor person in need of protection under IRPA sections 97(1)(a) and (b)

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 9 states the panel found claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection under IRPA.

propositions.text: Determinative issues are credibility and internal flight alternative (IFA)

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 10 states the determinative issues are credibility and internal flight alternative.

propositions.text: Panel aware of difficulties claimants face in hearings and stress in responding to questions
Panel considered passage of four and a half years since claimant's arrival in Canada

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 11 states panel considered claimant's hearing difficulties and time since arrival.

propositions.text: Panel found no glaring contradictions or inconsistencies in claimant's testimony
Panel found lack of evidence about claimant's circumstances since arrival in Canada
Panel must consider claimant's circumstances at hearing time given forward-looking refugee definition

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 12 states panel found no contradictions but lack of evidence post-arrival and must consider current circumstances.

propositions.text: Corroborative evidence confirms claimant's brother was killed
Mixed reports on whether assailants were apprehended and if brother was target
Claimant filed court documents to identify perpetrators, making him a target
Claimant believes no investigation outcome despite media reports suggesting otherwise
Claimant failed to provide evidence of ongoing investigation or pursuit since arrival in Canada
Claimant said sister and lawyer friends informed him of situation but gave no corroborative evidence

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 13 states panel found corroboration of brother's death but mixed reports, no evidence of ongoing risk or investigation, and no corroboration of claims about pursuit.

propositions.text: Panel gives benefit of doubt claimant would continue to be at risk in Santa Marta but no persuasive evidence
Panel examined viability of internal flight alternative (IFA)

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 14 states panel gave benefit of doubt on risk but found no persuasive evidence and examined IFA viability.

propositions.text: Panel finds viable internal flight alternative in Tunja, Boyacá, Colombia

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 15 states panel found a viable internal flight alternative in Tunja.

propositions.text: Test for viable IFA is two-pronged: no serious persecution risk and not objectively unreasonable to seek refuge there
Both prongs must be satisfied for IFA finding

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 16 states the two-pronged test for IFA: no serious risk and reasonable to seek refuge, both required.

propositions.text: Panel accepts on balance of probabilities that Urabeños are agent of persecution

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 17 states panel accepts Urabeños as agent of persecution.

propositions.text: Tunja is capital of Boyacá department

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 18 states Tunja is capital of Boyacá department.

propositions.text: Claimant testified he would be at risk from Urabeños in Tunja and not safe anywhere in Colombia
Claimant said Urabeños have widespread influence and means to track him down nationally

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 19 states claimant testified risk from Urabeños in Tunja and nationwide influence, as said by claimant.

propositions.text: National Documentation Package shows Urabeños do not have presence in Tunja
ELN responsible for two incidents in Boyacá in 2016 and 2017, no incidents in Tunja

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 20 states NDP shows Urabeños absent in Tunja; ELN responsible for incidents in Boyacá but none in Tunja.

propositions.text: NDP suggests Urabeños do not have presence in Boyacá or Tunja on balance of probabilities
In absence of credible evidence from claimant, objective documentation outweighs claimant's testimony
Claimant's information about Urabeños in Tunja comes from news, sister, and lawyer friends without corroboration
Claimant was unrepresented and strayed from questions, spoke generally about paramilitary groups
Potential threat from Urabeños does not extend to Tunja; no serious persecution or risk to claimant there

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds Urabeños not present in Tunja; claimant's uncorroborated testimony outweighed; no serious risk to claimant there, panel finds.

propositions.text: Claimant left Colombia end of 2014, questioned why Urabeños would pursue him now
Claimant insists Urabeños network can track him despite time lapse
Panel rejects claimant's assertion given objective evidence and lack of further evidence of pursuit

paragraphs.summary: Panel questioned claimant's claim Urabeños would pursue him now; claimant insists; panel rejects assertion due to lack of evidence.

propositions.text: Claimant does not face serious possibility of persecution or risk of torture, death, or cruel treatment if relocated to Tunja

paragraphs.summary: Panel finds claimant not at serious risk of persecution or harm if relocated to Tunja.

propositions.text: Proposed IFA of relocating to Tunja is not unreasonable in claimant's circumstances
Test for unreasonableness of IFA requires conditions jeopardizing life and safety
Actual and concrete evidence of such conditions must be presented

paragraphs.summary: Panel finds relocating to Tunja not unreasonable; test requires life-jeopardizing conditions and concrete evidence.

propositions.text: Claimant says moving to Tunja unreasonable because he cannot practice law there
Claimant acknowledges he cannot practice law in Canada either

paragraphs.summary: Claimant argues he cannot practice law in Tunja; acknowledges same in Canada.

propositions.text: No evidence claimant would have difficulty accessing healthcare in Tunja
Claimant is sophisticated and resourceful to support himself despite inability to practice law
Claimant's family situation changed; no longer with wife and son

paragraphs.summary: Panel finds no healthcare access issues; claimant resourceful; family situation changed.

propositions.text: Claimant has not established serious social, economic, or other barriers to relocating to Tunja
It would not be unreasonable for claimant to seek refuge in Tunja

paragraphs.summary: Panel finds claimant has not shown serious barriers; relocation to Tunja not unreasonable.

propositions.text: Insufficient evidence that Urabeños or other hazards make travel within Colombia to IFA unreasonable
Claimant may land at airport in Urabeños territory but Urabeños not actively seeking claimant
It would not be unreasonable for claimant to travel to Tunja by road or connecting flight

paragraphs.summary: Panel finds insufficient evidence hazards make travel unreasonable; claimant not actively pursued; travel to Tunja reasonable.

propositions.text: Claimant has a viable IFA in Tunja on balance of probabilities

paragraphs.summary: Panel finds claimant has a viable IFA in Tunja.

propositions.text: Claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor person in need of protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1)
Claimant does not face serious possibility of persecution or risk to life, cruel treatment, or torture on return
Claimant's claim is rejected

paragraphs.summary: Panel concludes claimant is not refugee or protected person; no serious risk on return; claim rejected.
